text:
maria: Quick proposal — want to land a progressive "shadow-swap" pattern for canary -> full. Idea: run new variant in parallel (mirror path) and progressively flip routing while keeping a secondary live path for fast rollback. Thinking about cache warmup, KV consistency, and telemetry gating.

kevin: +1 on the idea, but worried about double-write semantics for session affinity and KV cache. how do we avoid stale cache hits on the new path?

maria: Plan: 1) Start with read-only mirror (no writes to downstream stateful stores). 2) After warmup and acceptable telemetry, enable write-duplication behind a feature-flag. 3) Final route flip once cross-path divergence < threshold.

aj: Can we make the mirror path operate on an eventual-write buffer (write-ahead) that can be replayed if we decide to cutover? avoids duplicate side-effects until we commit.

lina: Sounds good. Need to define clear telemetry gates. What metrics? p50/p95 delta, error spike, misrouting rate, hallucination rate for certain prompts (ml signal).

maria: Exactly. Proposal for gating signals:
- functional correctness (sampled eval set failure rate)
- latency p95 delta <= 1.3x baseline
- error rate increase <= 0.2% absolute
- token-level quality regressions on canary prompt-set <= 1%

kevin: We also need to watch cache warmup curves — measure KV cache hit ratio over time and require stable slope before enabling writes.

maria: Agreed. Example config I threw together: 
```
canary: 
  mode: progressive-shadow-swap
  mirror_mode: read-only
  mirror_traffic_pct: 100
  warmup_window: 10m
  write_duplication_flag: off
  probes: 
    eval_sample_pct: 0.5
    telemetry_window: 5m
  rollback_triggers:
    p95_latency_multiplier: 1.3
    error_rate_pct: 0.2
    sample_eval_fail_rate: 1.0
```

aj: Nice. Suggest adding an explicit divergence detector that compares deterministic outputs (where applicable) and a fuzzy similarity score for non-deterministic ones.

devx: UX note: We should expose a live “shadow delta” dashboard in console showing side-by-side per-route metrics and an indicator for each gating signal (green/yellow/red). Also link to offending samples for quick triage.

lina: For escape hatches, recommend three levels: immediate cut (100% to old), gradual rollback (stop writes and drain mirror), and emergency quarantine (isolate both variants). Each should have runbook steps.

kevin: Edge-case: external side-effects (webhooks, billing). Must ensure idempotency or multiplex to a side-queue that dedups on commit.

maria: We'll add a side-queue mode for external effects during mirror runs; only commit to live systems on final cutover.

sre-bot: deploy-batch: canary-runner triggered for service:inference-runtime - run_id=20240207-17, started at 1719456833

maria: experiment plan: rollout to 5% tenant shadow for 24h, check gates, then enable write-dup for those tenants for another 6h, then promote to 25% real traffic with continued mirroring.

aj: +1. Also schedule a small chaos test (cpu spike + network flaps) to validate rollback logic during stress.

devx: I'll make a short console mock and a playbook; will link after noon.

kevin: One more: what about cost impact? Double inference cost while mirroring. Need to model token cost and set budget guardrails per tenant. If budget exceeded, auto-stop shadowing.

maria: Good call. Add budget guard with soft and hard limits. Soft = alert + reduce mirror pct, hard = stop mirror.

lina: For long-term, we should centralize the gating DSL so different teams can reuse the same signals and actions. RFC incoming.

maria: I'll draft RFC summarizing mechanic, gating signals, escape hatch runbooks, and API for feature-flagging write_duplication + side-queue commit. pinging @devx and @kevin for review.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary-config updated by maria in infra/canary-runs (PR 4121) — CI passed.

kevin: Reviewing PR now. small nit: rename `mirror_traffic_pct` to `mirror_mode_pct` so it's clear when mirror_mode!=read-only.

maria: good suggestion, will update. thanks all :thumbsup:

lina: LGTM once RFC + console mock link are posted.

maria: Thanks — will follow up with RFC link and schedule a sync next Tue.
